entities.name: Female genital tuberculosis
observations: Female genital tuberculosis can present with infertility, menstrual irregularity, abnormal uterine bleeding, and chronic pelvic discomfort.
Fallopian-tube involvement may cause peritubal adhesions, sinus-tract abnormalities, and impaired fertility.

entities.name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
observations: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the causative pathogen of female genital tuberculosis; menstrual fluid or endometrial material may be evaluated microbiologically.

entities.name: Infertility
observations: Infertility is a frequent presenting manifestation of female genital tuberculosis because of tubal and endometrial damage.

entities.name: Statins
observations: In a prospective ERSPC Aarau screening cohort, statin users had lower median PSA at baseline (1.5 vs 1.8 ng/mL) and follow-up (1.8 vs 2.1 ng/mL), but prostate-cancer incidence was not significantly different (7.4% vs 9.5%, p=0.08).

entities.name: Abnormal screening PSA
observations: Retrieved evidence did not provide an adjusted odds ratio or relative risk directly comparing statin users versus nonusers for PSA >4 ng/mL, abnormal PSA screening, PSA velocity, or biopsy referral.
A prospective false-positive PSA cohort used PSA >4.0 ng/mL as a biopsy indication, but statin use was not an independent predictor.
Systematic reviews retrieved did not pool abnormal screening PSA or biopsy-referral outcomes by statin exposure.

entities.name: PMID:39757796
observations: Prospective ERSPC Aarau screening cohort: 4,314 men, including 761 statin users, followed for a median of 9.6 years; statin users had lower PSA but no statistically significant difference in prostate-cancer incidence.

entities.name: PMID:36612257
observations: Prospective cohort of 1,664 men evaluating false-positive PSA results; PSA >4.0 ng/mL was a biopsy indication, but statin use was not reported as an independent predictor.
